the following issues: 1) the design of a test generator for datapath circuits, and 2) the design of test sets for IP cores.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

RIBTECs ATPG methodology is the most effective and efficient way to handle unimplemented blocks in the presence of unknown, unavailable, and/or changeable circuit implementations, and that RIBTECS test generation algorithm is the best way to generate test vectors for datapath circuits.
RIBTECs performance is superior in every way to that of the other ATPG programs.
RIBTECs ATPG is a very good solution for a very difficult problem, namely the ATPG of datapath circuits with unknown, unimplemented, or changeable IP blocks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel, effective, and highly practical approach to the problem of ATPG for unimplemented blocks.
RIBTEG is a very efficient tool for ATPG of datapath circuits with unknown blocks.
we can now design and test datapath circuits that employ unimplemented IP cores with a level of confidence that has been impossible before.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of a detailed circuit model, the functional (behavioral), rather than structural, fault model is the most effective for the purpose of high-coverage ATPG of unimplemented blocks in datapath circuits.
, in many cases, the high-level structure of a circuit can provide a sufficient basis for generating test sets with a very high level of fault coverage.
a high-level, realization-independent fault model can be constructed for datapath circuits and that such a model can be used to achieve a high level of testability for such circuits.
